guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: Barrick continues to expect 2026 gold production to be 2.90–3.25 million ounces1. Gold cost guidance for 2026 remains unchanged, including COS3 of $1,870–$2,070 per ounce, TCC4 of $1,330–$1,470 per ounce, and AISC4 of $1,760–$1,950 per ounce, based on a gold price assumption of $4,500 per ounce.

Copper production guidance for 2026 remains unchanged at 190,000–220,000 tonnes1. Copper cost guidance remains unchanged at COS6 of $3.05–$3.35 per pound, C1 cash costs4 of $2.20–$2.45 per pound, and AISC4 of $3.45–$3.75 per pound, based on a copper price assumption of $5.50 per pound.

Guidance is based on an oil price (WTI) assumption of $70 per barrel. For every $10 per barrel change in the oil price, the direct impact on costs associated with diesel consumption is approximately $12 per ounce across Barrick’s gold operations, and $0.04 per pound across its copper operations.

As previously disclosed, 2026 total attributable capital expenditure was reduced to $3.8 billion–$4.2 billion, from $4.0 billion–$4.45 billion, primarily reflecting lower anticipated spending at the Reko Diq project, which is under review.

desk.headline: Revenue up 22% to $5.07bn, just below estimates; adjusted EPS $0.82 beat; 2026 production and cost guidance reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose 22% to $5.07bn on a 23% higher realized gold price ($4,243/oz); adjusted EPS jumped 41% to $0.82, while IFRS EPS was $0.80.
Gold output was 816k oz, up 3% on Q2 but 2% lower than a year ago, hit by bad weather at Veladero and delayed high-grade ore at North Mara.
Costs climbed: gold all-in sustaining cost rose to $1,911/oz from $1,538 on lower grades, higher royalties and diesel; copper AISC rose to $4.52/lb.
Operating cash flow was $2.49bn, but attributable free cash flow fell 44% to $642m as capital spending rose.
Returned $1.04bn to shareholders ($761m buybacks plus a $0.175 dividend); net cash rose to $0.9bn from $0.3bn a year ago.

guidance.summary: Barrick kept its 2026 gold and copper production and cost ranges unchanged. The cut to attributable capital spending, mainly at Reko Diq, had already been announced before this report.

points: Management expects Q4 gold output to be slightly above Q3, with gold for the year landing around the middle of the range or a little higher.
Royalties and diesel remain the main cost pressures; copper costs are expected at the top end of guidance.
Barrick plans to file for the IPO of its North American assets this month, aiming to finish by year-end, possibly slipping into January.
Reko Diq spending has been slowed during the review, citing early review findings and security concerns; an update is expected by mid-2027.
No 2027 guidance yet; it will come with full-year results. Shareholder returns so far in 2026 total about $3.2bn.
